# `config default` for [env](/commands/categories/env.md)

<div class='command-title'>Show the default configuration.</div>

## Command Type

`built-in`

## Signature

```> config default {flags} ```


## Input/output types:

| input   | output |
| ------- | ------ |
| nothing | record |
## Examples

Show the name of the first default menu.
```nu
> config default | get menus | first | get name
completion_menu
```

Reset the keybindings to the defaults, then add one of your own. Assigning the defaults first keeps a config that is sourced again from growing the list.
```nu
> $env.config.keybindings = (config default).keybindings; $env.config.keybindings ++= [{ name: my_binding, modifier: control, keycode: char_t, mode: emacs, event: { send: clearscreen } }]

```

## Notes
The defaults nushell itself ships, whatever `$env.config` holds now. For `keybindings` and `menus` that is the list of entries nushell adds, such as the Tab completion menu, and not reedline's own base bindings (see `keybindings default`).
